title: Improve XML parsing throughput and allocations against BCL and native references
api_or_output: Measured compatible XML hot-path improvements, pinned BCL/libxml2/xmloxide comparisons and explicit measured feature-cost tradeoffs. Preserve all default XML correctness, diagnostics, quotas, source coordinates and earlier APIs; any public feature switch requires owning-contract follow-up.

acceptance.description: On all ten frozen XML fixtures, establish semantic-equivalent byte-DOM comparisons with current BCL, pinned libxml2 and xmloxide; record unmodified baseline, allocation/retention controls, native lifecycle differences, versions and raw local evidence outside tracked reports.

Improve raw throughput and allocations toward BCL parity: target geometric-mean latency and allocated-byte ratios <=1.10 and no per-fixture ratio >1.25 for the agreed equivalent default-feature profile; report every deficit honestly and do not relax semantics or exclude fixtures to claim parity.

Preserve default parsing, normalization, source mappings/locations, callbacks/pause/chunk boundaries, cancellation, quotas, DTD/entity provenance and recovery; pass focused and relevant cumulative tests plus task validation, with explicit allocation evidence for new borrowed primitives.

Inspect faster native/Rust implementations and quantify representative feature costs; document techniques to adopt and any proposed pay-for-play/default contract changes without dropping existing features silently.

handoff.summary: User-authorized performance lane after the measured current-main XML/BCL deficit; coordinator creates an explicitly owned repair task because no ready task existed.
remaining: Implement and measure default-compatible hot paths in isolated worktree.
